name: Entertainment venue (bowling, golf sim, etc.)
summary: Eatertainment boxes (bowling, golf simulators, arcade, full kitchen and bars) of ~25,000–50,000 SF, often in converted big-box retail. Building cost tracks RSMeans bowling/theater models; the big swing items are games/lanes/simulators (FF&E) and the level of interior design. Public-company capital data (Dave & Buster's: ~$16M per new store, ≈$480/SF all-in) bracket the all-in cost; hard cost is derived from that and RSMeans.

typicalSize.method: e4: D&B new stores averaged ~28,000 SF (target 25,000–45,000), Main Event ~50,000 SF. Independent bowling/sim venues often 15,000–25,000 SF. Mid 30,000.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Freestanding box at ~0.20–0.30 FAR with ~10 spaces per 1,000 SF surface parking. Derived.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Spaces per SF: entertainment/assembly zoning typically 6–12 per 1,000 SF; shared center parking common. Derived.

perPrimaryUnit.method: 2025 dollars. (a) RSMeans 2019 building hard cost bowling alley $167 union / $155 open shop (e1), movie theater $170 (e2); ×~1.30 to 2025 and +10% on-site work ≈ $220–240/SF for a plain new box. (b) D&B new-store capital ≈ $480/SF all-in (e3) × ~0.55 hard-cost share (remainder games/amusements, FF&E, kitchen equipment, soft) ≈ $265/SF. Mid $275 = (b) rounded up for eatertainment-grade interiors. Low $175 = conversion of an existing big box (interior + MEP); high $425 = ground-up, premium-design multi-level venue.

scope.notes: Building + interiors + typical on-site work. Excludes bowling lanes/pinsetters, simulators, arcade games, kitchen equipment, furniture (see lineItems/FF&E), land, soft costs, off-sites.

qualityTiers.method: economy = low/mid (175/275); luxury = high/mid (425/275 = 1.55); premium interpolated.

systemSplit.method: Derived: assembly/restaurant-type box with long-span roof (05), heavy interior finishes and feature ceilings (09 ≈ 13%), high HVAC for occupant density/kitchen (23 ≈ 11%), heavy power and lighting/AV backbone (26/27). On-site work ≈ 6%. Not sourced from a published estimate.

lineItems.name: Bowling lanes with string pinsetters, masking, scoring (per lane)

cost.method: Derived allowance for synthetic lanes, pinsetters, ball returns, scoring and masking units; boutique 'string' pinsetter lanes at the low/mid, free-fall at the high. Verify with Brunswick/QubicaAMF quotes.

lineItems.name: Golf simulator bay (launch monitor, projector, screen, enclosure)

cost.method: Derived allowance per commercial simulator bay including enclosure and installation.
Derived: D&B reports separate 'Games' capital lines (e3 table) indicating games are a material FF&E item; per SF of game floor, verify with vendor.
Derived allowance for full-service kitchen supporting 300–600 seats.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Furniture, bar fixtures, AV/TVs, signage (excluding games/lanes/simulators which are lineItems). D&B all-in ≈ $480/SF less hard ≈ $265/SF leaves ≈ $215/SF for games, FF&E, kitchen, soft; FF&E share assumed ~$45/SF.

pctOfHard.method: RSMeans model shows ~6% architectural fees (e1); plus MEP/food-service/AV consultants, permits, legal, insurance → ~12–25%. Derived.

softCosts.notes: Pre-opening costs are operating (D&B reports them separately) and not included.

hard.method: Higher end for big-box conversions with unknown existing conditions.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard + soft (excl. FF&E/games): low 175×1.1; high 425×1.25 ≈ 530, rounded.

source.title: Bowling Alley - Commercial Construction Costs Per Square Foot (RSMeans model page)
